description: Every deck measured by the lab and published. Use for 'best decks you can build' from a set of owned cards. 4868 decks were measured; 52 are not listed.

columns_doc.cards: 4 indices into the top-level `cards` array (sorted ascending); the deck is a set, board order is ignored
columns_doc.level: evidence level: 4 finals, 3 round-robin, 2 halving, 1 basic screen (see `levels`)
columns_doc.rate: native win rate at that level (draws count 1/2); NOT comparable between levels
columns_doc.rank_score: rate used to sort inside a level: equal to `rate` for levels 3-4 (equal game counts), shrunk toward the level mean for levels 1-2
columns_doc.halving_rounds_reached: level 2 only: halving rounds survived (1-3; more rounds = more games and a deck that passed more cuts); else null
columns_doc.tier_rank: rank in tierlist.json when the deck is in the top 30, else null

4.name: finals
4.description: strong AI, 200 games per pair against the 9 other finalists

3.name: round_robin
3.description: strong AI, 32 games per pair against the other decks of the 48-deck round-robin

2.name: halving
2.description: strong AI against the 8 probe decks, 24 to 168 games

1.name: screen
1.description: basic AI against 54 reference decks, 216 games

rank_key: Sort by `level` descending, then `rank_score` descending. Each higher level only contains decks that passed the cut of the level below (the funnel keeps the best), so a deck measured at a higher level is ranked above every deck that stopped earlier. Win rates of different levels use different opponents and AIs and must never be compared directly.

calibration.conclusion: Rank correlation between levels is weak or moderate on the decks that were measured at two levels (and those decks are pre-selected, which shrinks it further), so no common score is published; the evidence level is kept explicit.
